name: Cormac mac Cuilennain
bio: Cormac mac Cuilennain was king and bishop of Cashel, and is traditionally credited with the Psalter of Cashel and with the glossary known as Sanas Cormaic. Sigerson, in Bards of the Gael and Gall (1907), gives his dates as 837–903 and quotes O’Curry’s judgement that he was among the most distinguished scholars of his time; he is generally said to have been killed in battle in 908.

The poem “The Heavenly Pilot”, in which a sailor asks God to steer his frail boat, is taken from the Book of Leinster. Sigerson notes that it anticipates the thought of Tennyson’s “Crossing the Bar”. It is given here in his English version.

poems.title: The Heavenly Pilot
poems.author: Cormac mac Cuilennain
poems.collection: Bards of the Gael and Gall (1907)
poems.text:
Wilt Thou steer my frail black bark
O'er the dark broad ocean's foam?
Wilt Thou come, Lord, to my boat,
Where afloat, my will would roam?
Thine the mighty: Thine the small:
Thine to mark men fall, like rain;
God! wilt Thou grant aid to me
Who come o'er th' upheaving main?
